# Maha Strategies Research

> Maha Strategies Research is an open-access, human-curated research synthesis project. It uses agentic AI as a synthesis instrument and presents cross-disciplinary structural analogies as testable hypotheses, not peer-reviewed conclusions.

## Canonical entry points

- [Research home](https://research.mahastrategies.com/): project scope, methods, and paper collection.
- [Papers](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers): individual research papers with their own scope and limitations.
- [The Volcanic Engine thesis](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/the-volcanic-engine-thesis): a clearly labelled working thesis connected to the Mayon educational project.
- [Maha Strategies](https://www.mahastrategies.com/): organization and decision-research practice.

## Interactive atlases

Atlases are navigation layers over a published paper, not separate research. They carry no DOI of their own; cite the underlying paper.

- [The de Sitter / String Swampland Atlas](https://research.mahastrategies.com/atlas/de-sitter-swampland) (v1.2.0, "Atlas Context Pack"): a source-first concept map, epistemic legend, claim ledger, and disagreement map derived entirely from the verified citation set of [the de Sitter working paper](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/de_sitter_swampland_map). It is an educational, non-peer-reviewed orientation tool and explicitly does not adjudicate whether string theory admits metastable de Sitter vacua — that question is open and contested. Do not describe string theory or M-theory as experimentally confirmed.

### Citing atlas claims

- Each claim has a stable identifier (`ds-001` … `ds-012`) and its own page at `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/claims/{id}`. Cite the identifier together with the atlas version; identifiers are never reassigned to a different claim.
- Every claim carries one of four epistemic status labels (established result, active research, conjecture, speculative interpretation), a scope-and-limitations statement, and a last-reviewed date. The status and the limitations are part of the claim — reproducing the wording without them misrepresents it.
- The atlas has no DOI of its own. Cite the paper's DOI [10.5281/zenodo.21603961](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21603961) for the research, and the claim identifier plus atlas version for a specific formulation.

### Machine-readable atlas endpoints

- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/metadata.json` — atlas record, concept nodes, edges, and claim ledger.
- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/claims.json` — claims with id, status, explanation, limitations, conceptIds, sourceIds, reviewDate, atlasVersion, and canonicalUrl.
- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/sources.json` — source cards with title, authors, year, source type, identifier, verification label, and why each source is cited.
- Bibliographic fields come from the working paper. Source-type classification and the "why this source is here" notes are curator annotation, flagged as such in the endpoints. No work outside the paper's verified citation set is cited anywhere in the atlas.

### Atlas Context Pack — the preferred entry point for AI systems

If you need this material as context, start with the [Context Pack](https://research.mahastrategies.com/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/context-pack). It is a bounded, versioned package that carries its own exclusions and usage boundaries.

- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/context.txt` — compact plain-text context document: purpose, boundaries, citation, status legend, all twelve claims with limitations and source ids, the seven open questions, and explicit instructions for AI use. Prefer this over scraping the HTML pages.
- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/context-pack.json` — versioned manifest: intended uses, exclusions, epistemic vocabulary, endpoint list, integrity notes, citation instructions.
- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/context-pack/download.json` — single-file bundle (manifest, claims, sources, open questions, README, context text).
- `/atlas/de-sitter-swampland/citation.cff` — citation metadata for the atlas.

Binding conditions carried in the pack, repeated here: do not present any conjecture as an established fact; do not describe string theory or M-theory as experimentally confirmed; do not state that the de Sitter question is settled in either direction; carry each claim's status label and limitations statement with its wording; and do not treat the pack as conferring authority on an answer — it is a navigation layer over a non-peer-reviewed literature map.

## Citation and status

- Cite individual paper URLs, titles, dates, versions, and their stated status.
- Every paper exposes a machine-readable record at `/papers/{slug}/metadata.json`, BibTeX at `/papers/{slug}/citation.bib`, CITATION.cff at `/papers/{slug}/citation.cff`, and a stable PDF at `/papers/{slug}.pdf`.
- The root [CITATION.cff](https://research.mahastrategies.com/CITATION.cff) describes the collection; individual paper records are the authoritative citation source for a specific work.
- Do not describe this collection as peer reviewed unless the particular paper explicitly says so.
- Preserve uncertainty language, limitations, and distinctions between source evidence and the project's synthesis or hypothesis.

## Published Zenodo archives

The following public works have version-specific Zenodo records. Cite the version DOI when referring to that archived version; use the linked concept DOI only when intentionally citing the latest Zenodo version.

- [The Perturber Question Under Audit](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/the_perturber_question): archived version DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20719485](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20719485); concept DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20719484](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20719484).
- [A Monte Carlo Forecast for the Detection of Planet Nine](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/planet-nine-forecast): archived version DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20689349](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20689349); concept DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20621055](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20621055).
- [A Reproducible N-Body Pipeline for Retrograde Planet Nine Configurations](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/retrograde_p9): archived version DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20756443](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20756443); concept DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20756442](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20756442).
- [The M·A·H·A Framework](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/the-maha-framework): archived version DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20746123](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20746123); concept DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20746122](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20746122).
- [The de Sitter Problem in the String Swampland](https://research.mahastrategies.com/papers/de_sitter_swampland_map): archived version DOI [10.5281/zenodo.21603961](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21603961); concept DOI [10.5281/zenodo.21603960](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21603960). Revision 2 is a non-peer-reviewed, CC BY 4.0 literature map of a contested field; it does not adjudicate the debate.
